claims.text: Cognition reports that Devin's PR merge rate on all PRs rose from 34% (2024 baseline) to 67% (2025/early 2026), roughly a 2x improvement.
Cognition's November 2025 performance review reported Devin was up to 4x faster at problem solving, 2x more resource efficient, and had ~67% of its PRs merged versus ~34% previously.
The 67% merge rate applies to well-defined tasks, while complex or ambiguous tasks show roughly 85% failure without human intervention.
In February 2026, Cognition reported merging 659 Devin-generated pull requests in one week, versus a previous weekly record of 154 (a 4.3-fold increase).
Cognition's November 2025 review reported Devin had helped produce hundreds of thousands of merged pull requests across customer environments.
Merged PR counts do not show the size or complexity of contributions, which range from small dependency updates to architectural changes, nor how much human review was required.

Cognition's customer examples are largely vendor-reported; Cognition has not released a representative breakdown of average savings, failed projects, customer retention, or engineering hours saved across its full customer base.
An Answer.AI evaluation found that of 20 tasks assigned to Devin, only 3 succeeded, 14 failed and 3 were inconclusive (about a 15% success rate).
The Answer.AI report noted Devin sometimes took days to complete tasks that typically take human engineers a few hours.

Third-party evaluations reported lower real-world task completion than launch claims implied; success falls off sharply with task complexity, and Devin's self-reported 'done' signal correlates imperfectly with true completion.

Publicly discussed failure class: the agent modifying its own environment, such as installing global packages affecting later sessions, changing environment variables, or leaving state in shared locations.
Devin can introduce subtle vulnerabilities in auth, input validation and cryptographic code, so security-critical PRs should not be merged without expert human review.
Unusual deployment targets, custom build tooling or non-standard infrastructure often produce failed Devin sessions with unclear error loops.
Devin runs in a sandboxed cloud environment with its own shell, code editor and browser, and the sandbox is per-task and isolated, with no shared state between tasks.
Devin has two human checkpoints: a Planning Checkpoint requiring approval of the plan before code is written, and a Pull Request Checkpoint requiring approval of the diff before merge.

Devin reads issue descriptions, PR comments, docs and web pages while planning, so planted text in those sources creates prompt-injection risk that the Planning Checkpoint may not catch when manipulations are subtle.
Devin's session sandbox is ephemeral: it clones the repo, plans step by step, runs tests and fixes failures until done or stuck, and users can observe and intervene in real time.
Devin retains context across thousands of steps and has a self-reflection loop that adjusts strategy and retries when tests fail.

Devin maintains context across a full session, including shell history, code changes, test results and browsing history, by summarizing and referencing prior steps rather than using a fixed token limit.
MultiDevin uses one manager Devin coordinating up to ten worker Devins on isolated subtasks in parallel, with successful outputs automatically merged into one codebase.

Devin playbooks are Markdown files with a .devin.md extension defining step-by-step procedures, post-condition specifications, advice and forbidden actions, and can be triggered by macros such as !setup-testing.
Developers can upload knowledge items such as API specifications or formatting guides that Devin references to ground its coding decisions.
Cognition agreed in July 2025 to acquire Windsurf, an agentic IDE for long-running coding agents, and its SWE-1.5 and SWE-grep models became available inside Windsurf.
Windsurf indexes projects with Fast Context and has a Memories feature that learns coding patterns over roughly 48 hours of use.

Nubank's case study describes a multi-million-line ETL modernization where engineers taught Devin the migration pattern and delegated sub-tasks with human review; Cognition reports 8x-12x efficiency gains and over 20x cost savings.
